text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's new president Petar Stoyanov is expected to hand a mandate to the ruling Socialists to form a new government, leaders of the Socialist party and of the opposition said after having separate meetings with the president.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet gave approval to Bulgaria's state gas monopolist Bulgargas to join two Bulgarian joint stock companies and a Bulgarian-Russian joint firm.
-- Bulgaria's opposition demanded that the ruling Socialists gave up their mandate to form a new government and a caretaker cabinet was set up until early general elections were held in April.
-- A nationwide general political strike is expected to begin next week as a protest against the formation of a new Socialist cabinet, leaders of Bulgaria's main trade unions said.
-- The executive director of Bulgaria's state gas monopolist Bulgargas Petar Sabev was dismissed by the outgoing cabinet at his request because of poor health, a company official said.

-- The outgoing cabinet dismissed Kalin Mitrev from his post as executive director of the Mass Privatisation Centre. Mitrev was appointed two monts ago as Bulgaria's representative at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

-- Workers at Bulgaria's largest steel works Kremikovtsi held a protest rally against formation of a second socialist cabinet and demanded early general elections. Anti-government rallies and one-hour strikes were held across the country in the 17th day of protests.
-- Bulgaria's customs officers seized 14.7 kg of cocaine worth some $2 million and hidden in a Yugoslav-registered bus at the border checkpoint point of Kalotina.

-- Former central bank board member Gancho Kolev was elected as a member of the supervisory board of state-owned Biochim Bank, a bank official said. The bank posted a pre-tax profit of 66 billion levs for 1996 which would be fully set aside as provisions, the official added.
-- Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftohim would quit its participation in nine Bulgarian trade firms and a bank to ease the plant's financial crisis, the outgoing cabinet decided.
